_doc: Third-party files shipped inside the browser extension (SPEC-ext): extension/src/vendor, which extension/scripts/build.mjs copies into dist/<target>/vendor and so into the store packages (the Tabler SVGs become ui/icons.js, with their licence). go run ./scripts/licaudit checks: every file under extension/src/vendor is the NOTICE, a package's license_file or one of its files; a single file is pinned by sha256 (CRLF normalised to LF, like media.json); a glob of files names a text every matched file contains ({stem} = file name without extension), because the icon set changes with the interface; each license_file is recognised as the declared license; extension/src/vendor/NOTICE names exactly these packages with the same version, license, license file, source (the npm tarball), integrity and file SHA-256. That directory is excluded from the SPDX header check. npm packages of extension/package-lock.json are judged as shipped unless they are devDependencies (Playwright, end-to-end tests only). Paths are relative to extension/src/vendor.

packages.name: webextension-polyfill
packages.note: dist/browser-polyfill.js of the npm package, copied unchanged; it keeps its MPL-2.0 header (Exhibit A). MPL-2.0 is a file-level copyleft: the file is its own source form, and the package carries the license text (MPL-2.0 sections 3.1, 3.3: the extension as a larger work may be under the AGPL).

packages.name: @tabler/icons
packages.shipped_as: ui/icons.js (path data of the outline icons, with the MIT notice) and vendor/tabler/LICENSE
packages.note: icons/outline/*.svg of the npm package, unchanged in the repository; the build turns the path data into ui/icons.js.
